current_route.title: 24-layer HfO2/SiO2 dichroic with gradient thickness optimization and relaxed perturbation bounds
current_route.scientific_hypothesis: A 24-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 stack with individually tunable layer thicknesses can simultaneously achieve high reflectance in 300-450 nm and high transmittance in 1000-1700 nm at normal incidence on fused silica, with the gradient-thickness optimizer finding a non-quarter-wave solution that balances both bands.
current_route.design_principle: Recalled thin-film physics: dielectric mirrors use alternating high/low index layers to create photonic stopbands via constructive interference of reflections. Quarter-wave thicknesses (λ/4n) center stopbands at design wavelengths, but deviating from quarter-wave can broaden bands or create multiple passbands. HfO2 (high index ~2.0-2.1 in SWIR) and SiO2 (low index ~1.45) provide sufficient index contrast for reflectance in UV/blue while remaining transparent in SWIR.
current_route.proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate (24 coating layers total, alternating starting with HfO2 at air interface)
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 24 layers
thickness perturbation bounds ±18 nm for initial feasibility search
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
maximize mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band
maintain physical validity (no negative thicknesses, no material property violations)
manufacturing_considerations: total layer count fixed at 24 (within 30-layer limit)
all thicknesses must be positive and within depositor capability (20-200 nm range)
HfO2 and SiO2 are standard evaporatable/sputterable dielectrics
theory_basis: Recalled: Quarter-wave stacks produce stopbands centered at design wavelength; deviating from quarter-wave shifts and broadens stopbands.
Recalled: Index contrast between HfO2 and SiO2 is sufficient for high reflectance with ~12-15 layer pairs in UV/blue.
Recalled: Both HfO2 and SiO2 have low extinction coefficients in 1000-1700 nm, enabling high transmittance.
Recalled: Gradient-based thickness optimization can find local optima in multilayer design spaces when initialized near quarter-wave values.
Recalled: Normal incidence simplifies design as polarization splitting is not a factor.
expected_advantages: 24 layers provides sufficient degrees of freedom for dual-band optimization without exceeding manufacturing limits
Alternating high/low index pattern is a known working topology for dichroics
Gradient optimizer successfully produced target scores above 0.81 in prior iterations 04 and 12
Relaxed perturbation bounds (±18 nm vs ±12 nm) should increase feasible candidate yield
known_risks: Uncertain whether 24 layers is optimal vs 20 or 28 layers - this route does not explore layer count as a variable, so the true optimum pair count is unknown.
Uncertain exact refractive index values of hfo2 and sio2 datasets in the registry at 300 nm and 1700 nm endpoints - these are measured data, not design variables, but affect achievable performance.
Uncertain whether gradient optimizer will converge to global vs local optimum - multiple starting points would be needed to verify, but this route uses single initialization.
The ±18 nm perturbation bound is a hypothesis based on feedback directive; if it still produces zero valid candidates, the bound may need further relaxation or a different optimizer method.
No angle or polarization specified in original request - assumed normal incidence and unpolarized or average polarization; if actual use requires oblique angles, performance may degrade.
